title: Rotation runbook + audit evidence template for KMS/key rotation (SOC2/ISO aligned)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
description:
Define and publish (1) a repeatable key/KMS rotation runbook and (2) an audit-evidence-friendly template/checklist that Security + GRC + Eng can use to prove rotations occurred, were approved, and were monitored.

This ticket is specifically focused on the evidence artifacts + narratives needed for enterprise security reviews and audits (SOC 2 + ISO 27001), not on implementing the rotation mechanism itself.

Primary stakeholders:
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin, Hanae Suzuki, Kevin Osei
- GRC/Compliance: Olga Petrov, Daniel Carter
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Docs: Kira Thompson, Elliot Price

Outputs should be usable for:
- Internal quarterly rotations (Redwood-managed environments)
- Customer-driven rotations (Private deployments), where Redwood may provide process + tooling but customer executes parts of the change

Non-goals:
- Defining new cryptographic primitives
- Replacing existing change management systems (Linear/Jira); we’ll reference them as evidence sources

Acceptance criteria:
- A single “Rotation Evidence Packet” template exists (copy/paste friendly; can be stored as Confluence page + Drive doc) and is referenced from the runbook.
- Evidence packet includes: approvals, change tickets, timestamps, key identifiers (non-secret), audit log exports, and post-rotation verification.
- Explicit mapping section to SOC2/ISO narratives (what control the evidence supports + where it is produced).
- Clear split of responsibilities between Redwood operators vs Private customer operators.
- Includes instructions for generating evidence from systems we already have (audit log exporter / dashboards / CI runs), with screenshots/export guidance.
- Reviewed and approved by Security (Marcus) and GRC (Olga) and signed off by SRE readiness (Sean) for operational feasibility.

Deliverables:
1) Runbook: “KMS/Key Rotation Procedure + Verification + Rollback”
2) Template: “Rotation Log + Evidence Checklist (SOC2/ISO)”
3) Small appendix: “What auditors ask + how to answer” (Sales/SE-supportive, but primarily internal)

References (in-progress/related work):
- Epic: ENG-4821
- Error taxonomy/telemetry: ENG-4822, ENG-4828
- Game day outputs: ENG-4829
- Audit log events: PR redwood/pr-18541 (rotation-related audit events)
- Export schema: PR audit-log-exporter/pr-233 (rotation events in export)
- Docs page targeting: PR redwood-docs/pr-1294 (rotation procedure + evidence checklist)

Proposed “Rotation Evidence Packet” contents (template sections):
A. Summary
- Rotation name (e.g., “2025Q4 KMS KEK rotation – Hosted Control Plane”)
- Scope (Hosted/Dedicated/Private; which service(s); which regions)
- Rotation type (KEK rotation / DEK rewrap / key alias change / cutover flag flip)
- Planned window + actual execution start/end timestamps
- Ticket references (Linear ENG-####, change request ID, incident ID if any)

B. Approvals & Change Management
- Requestor
- Approver(s) + roles (Security approver, SRE approver, Customer approver for Private)
- Approval artifact links (Linear comment approval, Jira change, email thread if required)
- Risk assessment (brief) + rollback plan reference

C. Key Identifiers (non-secret) + Configuration
- KMS provider (AWS/GCP/Azure/HSM)
- Key ARN/Resource ID(s) (redacted format allowed if customer requires, but must be consistent)
- Key version(s) before/after (or alias target before/after)
- Services impacted (control-plane, data-plane, installer, etc.)
- Feature flags/config toggles used (e.g., dual-read enable, cutover enable)

D. Preconditions / Readiness Checks
- IAM policy validation completed (who/when; link to policy diff or Terraform plan)
- KMS health baseline captured (dashboard snapshot link; p50/p95 latency; error rate)
- Backups/escape hatches confirmed (break-glass procedure link; on-call coverage)

E. Execution Log (step-by-step, timestamped)
- Step name
- Operator
- Time
- Output (CLI output excerpt, dashboard screenshot, PR link, config diff link)

F. Verification Evidence (post-rotation)
- Audit log export showing rotation events (export timestamp + query filters)
- Service health checks green (include KMS healthcheck endpoint result where available)
- Error rates stable (KMS errors by taxonomy: AccessDenied/Throttling/Timeout/etc.)
- Functional smoke test results (decrypt/envelope operations succeed)
- For dual-read/cutover: confirmation that decrypt succeeds for N samples using both key versions (where applicable)

G. Rollback (if needed)
- If rollback executed: timestamp, reason, steps taken, verification after rollback
- If not executed: statement that rollback was not necessary + monitoring window duration

H. Incident / Exception Log
- Any incident tickets or near-miss notes
- Any exceptions requested (link to exception process doc) + compensating controls

I. Sign-off
- Security sign-off
- SRE sign-off
- Private customer sign-off (if applicable)
- Date/time

SOC2/ISO mapping (to include in the doc, high-level):
- SOC 2 Security (CC6.x access controls): approvals + IAM diffs + least privilege validation
- SOC 2 Change Management (CC8.1/CC8.2): change ticket, planned window, peer review, rollback plan
- SOC 2 System Operations (CC7.x): monitoring evidence, alerting, incident linkage if triggered
- ISO 27001 Annex A (2013 mapping; we can dual-reference 2022 if needed):
  - A.12.1 change management (change records)
  - A.12.4 logging and monitoring (audit log exports, dashboards)
  - A.9 access control (IAM least privilege evidence)
  - A.10 cryptography (key management procedures, rotation cadence)

Open questions to resolve in this ticket:
- What is the minimum acceptable evidence set for Private customers who cannot share raw key IDs/logs? (recommend a redaction policy + placeholder fields)
- Do we require screenshots, or are immutable exports preferred? (default to exports; screenshots as supplemental)
- Where does the template live as the source of truth (Confluence vs Drive vs docs repo)? Proposed: Confluence is canonical; Drive is “fillable”; docs site gets a sanitized customer-facing checklist.
- Who is the required approver set for each deployment mode? (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Definition of Done:
- Confluence page published under Security & Compliance > Runbooks/Standards and linked from the broader KMS rotation docs.
- Evidence template shared in Drive with a stable link and a version/date.
- At least one dry-run completed using the template (preferably aligned with ENG-4829 game day or a staging rotation), with “lessons learned” updates applied.
- Written acknowledgement in ticket comments from Marcus (Security) + Olga (GRC) + Sean (SRE) that the artifact meets their needs.
comments:
2025-10-28 (Talia Benson): Creating this as a standalone workstream because we keep getting ad-hoc asks from enterprise prospects for “proof of rotation” and “what does the evidence packet look like.” Need a template that Security + GRC can stand behind, and that eng can actually produce without heroics.

Owners: Daniel (evidence artifact), Olga (GRC review), Marcus (Security approval).

2025-11-01 (Daniel Carter): Drafted initial template structure (Summary / Approvals / Execution Log / Verification / Exports). Biggest gap: we don’t have a stable audit-log event taxonomy for rotation yet, so we can’t tell customers exactly what to export. Syncing with Kevin on what PR-18541 will emit (event names + fields).

2025-11-04 (Olga Petrov): From a SOC2 perspective, the evidence needs to show: (1) authorized change, (2) change executed as approved, (3) monitoring/verification after change, (4) exceptions handled. Don’t over-index on screenshots; prefer exportable artifacts with timestamps. For ISO narrative, be explicit that this is part of our “cryptographic key management” procedure.

Request: add a “redaction guidance” section for Private customers (acceptable to redact key ARN but must preserve uniqueness and show before/after).

2025-11-07 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure the template captures IAM policy scope validation + who validated it. We’ve had real-world AccessDenied incidents in Private where customers missed kms:Decrypt or encryption context constraints. Evidence packet should include “validation command output” OR “installer preflight report” once available.

Also add explicit “rollback criteria” + “rollback performed?” section; auditors ask what we do when things go wrong.

2025-11-09 (Sean Gallagher): SRE asks: keep it operable. Don’t require people to manually collect 12 dashboards. We should standardize on 2–3 core panels for before/after snapshots (KMS p95 latency, error rate by taxonomy, circuit breaker open rate if we expose it). If we can generate a single exported report from the observability pack later, we should call that out as a future improvement, but keep the first version manual + scoped.

2025-11-12 (Daniel Carter): Updated template with:
- “Private redaction policy” section
- Verification section now references the planned KMS health dashboard (ENG-4828) and rotation audit events (PR-18541 + exporter PR-233)
- Added mapping table: SOC2 CC8.1/CC8.2 for change mgmt + CC7.x for monitoring + ISO A.10/A.12.4

Next: schedule 30 min review with Marcus/Olga; then hand to Kira/Elliot to align wording with docs PR-1294.

2025-11-14 (Kira Thompson): From a docs perspective, recommend two outputs:
1) Internal runbook + full evidence packet template (includes internal system links, Linear/Jira process)
2) Customer-facing checklist (sanitized; describes what Redwood provides vs what the customer must capture)

I’ll add a “Responsibilities matrix” table in the draft and route it for review in the docs PR.
